## Fatal findings

None.

## Nonfatal findings

### 1. `thm-sylow-third-theorem` | Step 1.1, and the item’s dependency list | Existence of a Sylow subgroup is silently assumed

**What is wrong:** Step 1.1 opens “Let a Sylow subgroup \(P\) act by conjugation on the Sylow set.” This assumes \(\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)\) is nonempty, i.e. it silently invokes Sylow I. None of the item’s cited dependencies proves existence. `thm-sylow-second-theorem` and `thm-sylow-number-as-normalizer-index` both begin with a chosen Sylow subgroup \(P\), and `def-number-of-sylow-p-subgroups` only defines \(n_p(G)\) and says the first theorem “later shows it is nonzero.” The item’s `deps` do not include `thm-sylow-first-theorem`.

**Evidence:** The `deps` field is
`[thm-sylow-second-theorem, thm-sylow-number-as-normalizer-index, thm-p-group-fixed-point-congruence, def-number-of-sylow-p-subgroups, lem-product-with-normal-subgroup]`.
The supplied dependency text for `thm-sylow-second-theorem` begins:
“Let \(G\) be finite, let \(P\) be a Sylow \(p\)-subgroup …”
and the item’s [L4] says only:
“… thm-sylow-first-theorem later shows it is nonzero.”

**Why nonfatal:** The statement is true, and a reader can repair the proof in seconds by citing `thm-sylow-first-theorem` before choosing \(P\). The gap is in the proof/dependency trace, not in the mathematical claim.

## Boundary checks

- `thm-sylow-third-theorem`: For \(|G|=1\), one has \(a=0\), \(m=1\), and \(n_p(G)=1\), so \(1\equiv 1\pmod p\) and \(1\mid 1\). More generally, if \(p\nmid |G|\), then \(n_p(G)=1\). No \(n=0\)/\(n=1\) parameter is present. The statement is one-way, not an iff. The only boundary caveat is the nonemptiness of \(\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)\), covered by the nonfatal finding above.
- `cor-normal-sylow-subgroup-of-a-normal-subgroup-is-normal`: For \(N=1\), \(P=1\) and \(1\trianglelefteq G\). The statement is one-way; the only iff in the item is [L1], and only its forward direction is used. No boundary defect found.
- `lem-distinct-normal-sylow-subgroups-commute`: In the trivial group, for distinct primes \(p,q\), the trivial subgroup is both the \(p\)- and \(q\)-Sylow subgroup, and the trivial commutator is trivial. If one Sylow order is \(1\), the same argument applies. The statement is not an iff. No boundary defect found.

## Citation accuracy

All \([L\#]\) restatements in the three items were checked against the supplied dependency texts. I found no inaccurate restatement or inflated dependency. Item 1 cites `lem-product-with-normal-subgroup` ([L5]) though the proof does not use it; that is extraneous but not a defect in the claimed result.

## Coverage

I read fully:

- `thm-sylow-third-theorem`
- `cor-normal-sylow-subgroup-of-a-normal-subgroup-is-normal`
- `lem-distinct-normal-sylow-subgroups-commute`

and all dependency texts supplied with the dispatch. I checked every cited dependency restatement against its supplied text. I could not check dependency provenance flags for the cited items, since those flags were not reproduced; the three reviewed items’ own statements are marked `literature-derived`.
